sections.overview: This small swift is widespread across tropical South and Southeast Asia and is strongly associated with palms.
sections.identification: It has long swept-back wings and a deeply forked tail, and spends most of its life flying rather than perching.
sections.habitat: It uses open country, clearings and cultivation, especially where palms or areca nut trees provide nesting sites.
sections.diet: It catches small flying insects in the air, often foraging around palms and over open ground.
sections.behavior: It is usually seen in small flocks and clings to vertical surfaces with its short feet instead of settling on the ground.
sections.reproduction: The tiny nest is glued to the underside of a palm leaf with saliva, and the eggs are secured to the nest.
sections.ecology: It was formerly combined with the African Palm Swift Cypsiurus parvus, but the two are now treated as separate species.
sections.conservation: The 2024 global assessment lists it as Least Concern, reflecting its very large range rather than the condition of every local population.
